title: Bridging the Language Gap in Scholarly Data II: Enhancing Gender Inference for Chinese Names
abstract: arXiv:2610.23734v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Perceived gender inference from names is important for inclusive scientometrics research, yet existing methods perform poorly on non-Western scholars. We address this gap for Chinese names, which appear in two forms, Hanzi and Pinyin, its Romanized form (e.g., Zhang Wei, Li Na). In international bibliographic records, names are often available only in Pinyin. However, a single pinyin name can correspond to multiple distinct hanzi characters with different gender associations, so gender inference from Pinyin alone is intrinsically ambiguous. To address this, we first develop two hanzi models, a regression model that produces a continuous gender score from 0 (male) to 1 (female), and a classification model that outputs one of three labels (\em{male}, \em{neutral}, \em{female}). We train them on a sample of hanzi names from Chinese-language physics publications, rated by 11 native Chinese speakers. On this sample, the models achieve an RMSE

translated_title: 弥合学术数据中的语言鸿沟（二）：提升中文姓名的性别推断
translated_abstract: 从姓名推断感知性别对于包容性的科学计量学研究十分重要，然而现有方法在非西方学者身上表现较差。我们针对中文姓名来解决这一缺口。中文姓名存在两种形式：汉字和拼音（其罗马化形式，例如 Zhang Wei、Li Na）。在国际书目记录中，姓名通常仅有拼音形式。然而，同一个拼音名字可能对应多个具有不同性别联想的汉字，因此仅凭拼音进行性别推断在本质上是模糊的。为解决这一问题，我们首先开发了两个汉字模型：一个回归模型，输出从0（男性）到1（女性）的连续性别得分；一个分类模型，输出三个标签之一（男性、中性、女性）。我们在来自中文物理学出版物的汉字姓名样本上训练这些模型，该样本由11位中文母语者进行评分。在该样本上，模型取得了RMSE……
tldr: 针对拼音中文姓名性别推断固有的模糊性问题，该研究开发了由11位中文母语者评分数据训练的汉字回归与分类性别推断模型，以提升科学计量学研究中对中文学者姓名的性别推断准确性。
en_tdlr: To address the inherent ambiguity of gender inference from Pinyin-only Chinese names, this study develops hanzi-based regression and classification models trained on ratings from 11 native Chinese speakers, improving gender inference for Chinese scholars in scientometrics research.
